title: Building a complete basic repertoire
summary: One system as White and two defences as Black, 8-10 moves deep with typical plans and model games, kept in a file you review after every game.

steps.md: Stage-3 guidance (1000-1400): **fix one White system and two Black defences** (one vs 1.e4, one vs 1.d4), know **8-10 moves** of the main lines, the **typical middlegame plan**, and **2-3 model games** per line. After every game, compare your opening with the database and patch the file. Spend most training time on tactics and endgames: openings matter, but less than you think at this level.

steps.question: Which repertoire best fits these guidelines?
choices: White: 1.e4 Italian + a simple anti-Sicilian; Black: 1...e5 vs 1.e4 and the QGD vs 1.d4
White: five different first moves; Black: a new defence every week
Only gambits, everything memorised 25 moves deep
steps.explain: Compact, principled and consistent: one system, two defences, with understanding.

steps.prompt: Your Italian file, move 8 for Black. Play a typical plan move: prepare to bring the knight to the kingside or challenge the centre.
steps.explain: ...a6 keeps the bishop pair after a possible Na5 and prepares ...Ba7-type ideas; ...Na5, ...Be6 and ...h6 are also normal. In your file, note the plan, not just the move.

steps.prompt: Your QGD file as Black. Play the main-line move that prepares ...Nbd7 or ...b6 with ...h6 options.
steps.explain: ...h6 asks the bishop to decide (Bh4 or Bxf6) before Black chooses a set-up: Tartakower (...b6) or Lasker (...Ne4). ...Nbd7 is also standard.

steps.question: After a tournament game you find the opponent deviated on move 6 and you did not know the line. What is the right repertoire workflow?
choices: Look up the deviation in a database, add 1-2 reliable answers and the plan to your file, then review it with spaced repetition
steps.explain: A repertoire grows from your own games. Spaced repetition (MoveTrainer style) keeps it in memory.

steps.question: How deep should a stage-3 player know main lines?
choices: About 8-10 moves, with the typical plans
steps.explain: Depth beyond that pays off only from stage 4-5 onwards.

steps.question: Which is the best way to make opening study stick?
choices: Quizzing yourself on the moves and plans (retrieval), spaced over days, and playing the lines in training games
steps.explain: Retrieval practice beats re-reading. Play the lines against bots and review the games.

steps.question: Retrieval check: what are the three ingredients of each repertoire line?
choices: Main-line moves (8-10), the typical middlegame plan, and 2-3 model games
steps.explain: Plans and model games are what let you play sensibly once theory ends.
